SPACE had no effect on the yellow (Z1's top bar is still 18px). The timer decreased (8→7).
In other words, SPACE is not the absorption trigger (or it's irrelevant).
Let me reconsider. In level 2, the clear occurred on the LEFT move that brought the charcoal to (42,9,53,23). What was special about that position? The charcoal's left edge c9 = the yellow's... the yellow is c3-17. The charcoal covered c9-17 (the right 9 out of 15 columns). The yellow's center c10 was covered.
Level 3's T on Z1: T (12,9,17,20) covers c9-20 = all of Z1's columns (Z1 is c9-20). The T's top bar covers the entire bottom bar. The T's rows r12-17 vs Z1's rows r9-14: the T covers r12-14 of Z1 (the bottom bar) — the bottom half.
Level 2: the charcoal covered the right half (columns) of the yellow. Level 3's T covers the bottom half (rows) of Z1. Both cover half. Level 2 cleared, level 3 didn't.
Difference: in level 2, the charcoal's shape was 12×12 (72px), and the yellow was 12×15 (72px) — the charcoal is a big square-ish piece. Level 3's T is 48px.
Hmm, maybe the clear condition is that the dark piece covers the yellow's center pixel? Level 2: yellow's center (47.5, 10); the charcoal covers c9-23 r42-53 → contains (47.5,10) ✓. Level 3's Z1: center (11.5, 14.5); the T covers r12-17 c9-20 → r11.5 is not covered (the T starts at r12) ✗. So the T needs to shift up by 1 to cover r11.5? But the movement is in units of 3 — you can't shift by 1.
Or maybe the condition is that the yellow's center is within the dark piece's bounding box, and the dark piece's center is within the yellow's bounding box?
Level 3's T center (14.5, 14.5); Z1's bbox r9-14 c9-20: T center r14.5 > 14 ✗.
Hmm, the movement granularity is 3, so the T's rows are r12-17 (top edge r12). Z1's rows are r9-14. For the T's top edge to be at r9: T (9,9,14,20): top bar r9-11 on top of Z1's top bar (c12-17 vs c12-20: 18px overlap), stub r12-14 c12-17 on top of Z1's bottom bar (c9-20: 18px overlap). This is a better interlocking fit! T's top bar on top of Z1's top bar, stub on top of Z1's bottom bar. Overlap = 36px, covering both bars.
From (12,9): 1 UP → (9,9,14,20). Let's try that!
No wait, is that really a better "fit"? T: top bar 12 wide, stub 6 wide. Z1: top bar 9 wide (c12-20), bottom bar 12 wide (c9-20). T at (9,9): top bar r9-11 c9-20 covers Z1's top bar c12-20 (9 out of 12) ✓; stub r12-14 c12-17 covers part of the bottom bar (6 out of 12). Total overlap: 27+18=45px?? The T is only 48px: top bar 36 + stub 18 = 54? No: T = 48px = top bar 12×3=36 + stub 6×3=18 → 54? That's 54, not 48. Hmm, T's pixels=48. So the T's top bar is 12×3=36, stub is 4×3=12? Or the top bar is 36 and the stub is 12 (4 wide). Bbox (12,9,17,20): 6 rows × 12 cols. 48px = 36 (top bar) + 12 (stub 4×3, c12-15?). The stub is c12-15 (4 wide), not c12-17.
Whatever — the exact stub width is 4. T at (9,9,14,20): overlap with Z1 = top bar r9-11 ∩ Z1 top bar r9-11 c12-20 = c12-20 (9 cols × 3 = 27) + stub r12-14 c12-15 ∩ Z1 bottom bar = 12. Total 39px of the 48.
Versus the current position (12,9): top bar r12-14 c9-20 ∩ Z1 bottom bar r12-14 c9-20 = 36px + stub r15-17 (nothing). Overlap 36px.
So (9,9) has more overlap (39 vs 36) and covers both bars. Let's try 1 UP.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def yinfo(f):
    seg = f.segmentation
    out = []
    for n in seg['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='Y' and n['pixels']>5:
            b=n['boundary']
            r0=min(p[0] for p in b); r1=max(p[0] for p in b); c0=min(p[1] for p in b); c1=max(p[1] for p in b)
            out.append((r0,c0,r1,c1,n['pixels']))
    return out
def binfo(f):
    seg = f.segmentation
    out = []
    for n in seg['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='B' and 30 < n['pixels'] < 100:
            b=n['boundary']
            r0=min(p[0] for p in b); r1=max(p[0] for p in b); c0=min(p[1] for p in b); c1=max(p[1] for p in b)
            out.append((r0,c0,r1,c1,n['pixels']))
    return out
res = action(['UP'])
print('Y:', yinfo(current_frame), 'B:', binfo(current_frame))
print('done:', last_action_result.get('done'), 'lvl:', last_action_result.get('level_completed'), 'step:', current_frame.step)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
